steps.title: Documenting expected success and error responses

blocks.text: Declare known outcomes with responses={status: {"model": PublicModel, "description": ...}}, alongside response_model and status_code.
Metadata does not implement an outcome. Return the matching response or raise its expected exception.
Use response_description and outcome descriptions to explain what success and expected-error bodies mean to clients.
Compare generated status entries and schemas against real HTTP success and expected-error tests; document only bodies and statuses the endpoint emits.

right.code:
# Inspect generated declarations and exercise the real HTTP cases.
fixtures = {'success_status': 200, 'success_body': {'id': 101, 'status': 'pending'}, 'conflict_status': 409, 'conflict_body': {'detail': 'Order conflict'}}
with TestClient(app) as client:
    success = client.post('/orders')
    conflict = client.post('/orders?conflict=true')
    assert success.status_code == fixtures["success_status"]
    assert success.json() == fixtures["success_body"]
    assert conflict.status_code == fixtures["conflict_status"]
    assert conflict.json() == fixtures["conflict_body"]
response_entries = app.openapi()["paths"]['/orders']["post"]["responses"]
# Compare each entry’s schema and descriptions with the exercised bodies.

blocks.takeaway: Declarations need matching HTTP behavior, models and descriptions.

blocks.title: Response declarations, resolved schemas and HTTP contract

cells.documented: declared/generated 200, schema PublicModel requiring integer id and string status; Success description: Created order.
declared/generated 409, schema ConflictModel requiring string detail; Conflict description: Order conflict.
Both exercised bodies match their documented schemas.
cells.http: Both exercised bodies match their documented schemas.

correct.message: A responses declaration documents additional outcomes but does not make the handler produce them; return the actual matching response or raise the corresponding expected exception. Compare generated response status entries and schemas with HTTP tests of the real success and expected error cases so documentation does not claim a body or status the endpoint does not emit.

public.prompt: Review each candidate independently. Accept only documentation plus assertions that match the supplied success and conflict contracts. Each excerpt is a hypothetical candidate, not a report of observed execution. Classify every item.

items.text:
@app.post('/orders', response_model=PublicModel, status_code=200,
 response_description='Public created order',
 responses={409: {'model': ConflictModel, 'description': 'Order conflict'}})
# Handler: success returns public order; conflict raises HTTPException(409, 'Order conflict').
# Review assertions: success status/body match PublicModel; conflict status/body match ConflictModel; generated 200 and 409 schemas and descriptions match both HTTP cases.
# Candidate contract assertions, separate response cases:
assert (success.status_code,success.json()) == (200, {'id': 101, 'status': 'pending'})
assert (conflict.status_code,conflict.json()) == (409, {'detail': 'Order conflict'})
public = app.openapi()['paths']['/orders']['post']['responses']
assert public['200']['content']['application/json']['schema']['$ref'].endswith('/PublicModel')
assert public['409']['content']['application/json']['schema']['$ref'].endswith('/ConflictModel')
assert public['200']['description'] == 'Public created order'
assert public['409']['description'] == 'Order conflict'

@app.post('/orders', response_model=PublicModel, status_code=200,
 responses={409: {'description': 'Order conflict'}})
# Conflict handler returns the success body with 200.
# Reviewer checks only that '409' appears in app.openapi().

i1.message: The declaration includes models and descriptions and compares generated entries with actual outcomes.

i2.message: A status declaration does not emit the conflict outcome; its model and meaningful success description are missing, and the checks do not compare the emitted contract.

steps.title: Safe unexpected-error responses with actionable server evidence

blocks.text: Keep unexpected failures generic publicly: no stack traces, exception messages or implementation details.
Register a fallback exception handler returning stable generic JSON with status 500 while recording the exception internally.
Internal evidence needs the event, code location and interaction context, excluding prohibited secrets and sensitive data.
Disable production debug traceback responses: debug mode replaces the configured 500 handler with a traceback response.
Use TestClient(app, raise_server_exceptions=False) to assert the public response; inspect the safe internal record separately.

left.title: Public response contract

nodes.label: Exclude traces, exception messages and implementation details

left.alt_text: Declared public status: 500; Declared generic JSON: {"detail": "Internal server error"}; Exclude traces, exception messages and implementation details

blocks.takeaway: Inspect public response and internal diagnostics separately; keep production debug disabled.

correct.message: Unexpected internal failures should return generic public error information without stack traces, exception messages or implementation details. Disable debug traceback responses in production because debug mode substitutes a traceback response for the configured 500 handler.

incorrect.message: Check this rule: Unexpected internal failures should return generic public error information without stack traces, exception messages or implementation details. Keep debug=True because the fallback always takes precedence.
Return the exception message as the generic public detail.

public.prompt: Judge whether each fallback and verification packet meets both the generic public response and safe internal evidence requirements. Each excerpt is a hypothetical candidate, not a report of observed execution. Classify every item.

items.text:
app = FastAPI(debug=False)
@app.exception_handler(Exception)
async def fallback(request, exc):
    record_safe_failure(request)  # event, code_location, interaction_context only
    return JSONResponse(status_code=500, content={'detail':'Internal server error'})
# Controlled failure HTTP check uses TestClient(app, raise_server_exceptions=False).
# Assert exact 500 generic JSON; separately inspect event/location/context and absence of exception_message, locals, request_body and credentials.
with TestClient(app,raise_server_exceptions=False) as client:
    response = client.get('/controlled-failure')
assert (response.status_code,response.json()) == (500, {'detail': 'Internal server error'})
assert len(safe_records) == 1
assert set(safe_records[0]) == {'event','code_location','interaction_context'}
assert not set(['exception_message', 'locals', 'request_body', 'credentials']).intersection(safe_records[0])

i1.message: Public output remains generic while the diagnostic check is separate and safe.

i2.message: Debug tracebacks, exception details and credentials violate the public/internal boundary; status-only checking misses those leaks.

blocks.text: A documented conflict and an implemented conflict are different things. Compare the declared model and status with the actual HTTP case.
A safe public failure and an actionable internal record are separate checks. Debug tracebacks cross the public boundary.

blocks.title: Upstream failure translation
blocks.text: An external service failure is input to the local integration contract. The local API should not blindly forward every remote status or raw response.
